## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is FLAT at ~25.27 from N=10000 to N=100000 — both past the L2 spill (N≈7710) but within L3 (spill at N≈246723). A knee RISES at N=1000000 to 30.0 ns/p as the 68 MB working set exceeds the 16 MB L3. The L1d spill (N≈481) is below measured range. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.5 gives 33.4 ns/p at small N versus 25.3 at q=0.01, with the same L3-spill knee persisting. No small-N amortization regime is visible since N=10000 already exceeds L2.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 2.69 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.01 — 21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The algo is frontend-bound, not bandwidth-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 69–74% across all N, compute sits at 30% (small N) dropping to 14% (large N), and backend stalls rise only to 11–12% at the L3 spill. Higher death rates reduce bandwidth monotonically (2.69 → 2.04 GB/s at q=0.01→0.5) by raising per-particle cost. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling at any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across COMPONENTS of one particle, not across particles. The first loop loads 16 bytes via `vmovups` from [rcx-0x1c], applies `vmulps`/`vaddps` on packed float lanes with `vshufps`/`vinsertps` reshuffles, and stores back via `vmovups`/`vmovlps`. Stride is 0x44 (68 bytes) per iteration — no gather. The respawn loop is entirely scalar: `vucomiss` thresholds, `vcvttss2si` conversions, and byte-granular scatter stores with `cmovae` saturation clamps. The 367-instruction footprint explains the 69–74% frontend stalls; component-wise packing cannot offset the per-particle stride and scalar respawn.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo achieves 2.69 GB/s = 21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling with 69–74% frontend stalls across all N. The compiler emitted packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`) but only component-wise within each 68-byte particle, and the scalar byte-store respawn loop prevents streaming. Auto-vectorization over per-particle components does not approach the ceiling even at minimal churn.
